title: である and the older copulas
summary: である is the plain, straight copula; だ and です are its short forms, and でございます is its polite version.

blocks.text: **である** is the copula in its full form. Historically だ is a short で + ある, and です is a short であります. You meet である in essays, news and textbooks, because it is neutral: neither casual (だ) nor polite (です).

rows: で + ござる (polite ある) + ます
で + ござる (polite ある)

blocks.text: The copula puts noun A inside the set named by noun B. The particle **で** draws a boundary ("within which") and **ある** means to exist, so で + ある means "exists within this boundary". Do not confuse the particle で with the て-form of the copula, which is also で.
The big use: before a noun
だ and です can only end a clause. Only a な-noun can modify a noun, with な. For any other noun, である is the one way to build a modifier:

blocks.jp: 医者である父は忙しい。
blocks.en: My father, who is a doctor, is busy.

blocks.text: 医者である父は忙しい。 The describer sits in front of 父, and only 忙しい is the engine.
Compare 医者の父 ("doctor father"), which is vaguer. And 丸のさま does not work, so we need である.

English uses "is" for both. Japanese keeps them apart: **copula** (これは猫だ, this belongs to the set "cat") versus **ある / いる** (庭に猫がいる, a cat exists there). Japanese teachers call the copula a kind of verb; this course keeps it as its own third engine, because it has its own て-form (で) and its own linking form (な).

items: だ = casual, です = polite, である = plain and written.
である can modify a noun; だ and です cannot.
The copula says "A belongs to set B"; ある says "A exists".

questions.instruction: What register is である?
questions.note: である is neither casual (だ) nor polite (です).

questions.instruction: Which form is very polite, used in shops and announcements?
questions.note: でございます is the very polite copula.

questions.instruction: Which form can modify a noun that is not a な-noun?
questions.note: だ and です only end a clause; である builds a modifier.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 学生＿＿＿弟は、毎日勉強している。
questions.note: である lets a noun modify the next noun.
questions.en: My younger brother, who is a student, studies every day.

questions.instruction: Which sentence states plainly that Mother is a teacher?
options: 先生である母は優しい
questions.note: である states it plainly; の is vaguer.

questions.instruction: Which form can only end a clause?
questions.note: だ and です end a clause; である can sit before a noun.

questions.instruction: What does であります add to である?
questions.note: であります is である + ます.

questions.instruction: What is the で in である?
options: The particle で, drawing a boundary
questions.note: で + ある: exists within the boundary.

questions.instruction: Which sentence suits a news report?
questions.note: である is neutral and written.

questions.instruction: What does ある say?
options: That A belongs to set B
questions.note: ある / いる are verbs of existence.

questions.instruction: Which sentence uses the copula, not existence?
questions.note: これは猫である puts it in the set "cat".

questions.instruction: Which sentence builds a modifier correctly?
questions.note: である + noun is the way to modify with a plain noun.

questions.instruction: Tap the copula
questions.note: である is the full-form copula.

questions.instruction: Tap the noun that である attaches to
questions.note: 先生 + である modifies 母.
questions.en: My mother, who is a teacher, is busy.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: My older brother, who is a student, lives near the school.
questions.note: である lets 学生 modify 兄.
questions.en: My older brother, who is a student, lives near the school.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.note: Noun + である ends the sentence in a plain written style.

questions.instruction: Why does the course keep the copula as its own engine?
options: It has its own て-form and linking form
questions.note: Its て-form is で and its linking form is な.

questions.instruction: Which is the polite version of である, the long form behind です?
questions.note: であります is the polite version of である.

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: The particle で and the て-form of the copula are the same thing.
questions.note: They look the same but do different jobs.

questions.instruction: Compare 先生の母 and 先生である母. Which is vaguer?
questions.note: である states plainly that she is a teacher; の is vaguer.

questions.instruction: Which needs である before a noun?
questions.note: 静か is a な-noun and takes な; 学生 needs である.

questions.instruction: Which word hides inside でございます?
questions.note: でございます is で + ござる + ます.

questions.instruction: Which copula would a samurai in a period drama use?
questions.note: でござる is the old-fashioned form from period dramas.
